questions.a: Copper is smelted out of stone.

questions.q: What does man search out to the farthest limit?
questions.a: Man searches out, to the farthest limit, the stones of gloom and thick darkness.

questions.q: Where does man break open a shaft?
questions.a: He breaks open a shaft away from where people live.

questions.q: What is contained in the dust of the earth?
What has not walked through the path of man’s shaft?
questions.a: The proud animals have not walked such a path, nor has the fierce lion passed there.

questions.q: What does man see in the channels he cuts among the rocks?
questions.a: His eye sees every valuable thing there.

questions.q: Where are wisdom and understanding not found?
questions.a: Both of these are not found in the land of the living.

questions.q: What cannot equal the worth of wisdom and understanding?
questions.a: Gold and crystal cannot equal both of these in worth.

questions.q: The price of wisdom is more than what jewel?
questions.a: The price of wisdom is more than rubies.

questions.q: From whose eyes is wisdom hidden?
questions.a: Wisdom is hidden from the eyes of all living things.
God understands the way to wisdom and he knows its place.

questions.q: What did God parcel out by measure?
questions.a: He parceled out the waters by measure.

questions.q: For what did God make a decree?
questions.a: He made a decree for the rain.

questions.q: What did God tell people is wisdom?
questions.a: To people, God said, “See, the fear of the Lord—that is wisdom.”

commentary.text: Wisdom is the gift of God.

Verses 1–11 Job maintained that the dispensations of Providence were regulated by the highest wisdom. To confirm this, he showed of what a great deal of knowledge and wealth men may make themselves masters. The caverns of the earth may be discovered, but not the counsels of Heaven. Go to the miners, thou sluggard in religion, consider their ways, and be wise. Let their courage and diligence in seeking the wealth that perishes, shame us out of slothfulness and faint-heartedness in labouring for the true riches. How much better is it to get wisdom than gold! How much easier, and safer! Yet gold is sought for, but grace neglected. Will the hopes of precious things out of the earth, so men call them, though really they are paltry and perishing, be such a spur to industry, and shall not the certain prospect of truly precious things in heaven be much more so?

Job here speaks of wisdom and understanding, the knowing and enjoying of God and ourselves. Its worth is infinitely more than all the riches in this world. It is a gift of the Holy Ghost which cannot be bought with money. Let that which is most precious in God's account, be so in ours. Job asks after it as one that truly desired to find it, and despaired of finding it any where but in God; any way but by Divine revelation. (Job 28:20-28)

There is a two-fold wisdom; one hid in God, which is secret, and belongs not to us; the other made known by him, and revealed to man. One day's events, and one man's affairs, have such reference to, and so hang one upon another, that He only, to whom all is open, and who sees the whole at one view, can rightly judge of every part. But the knowledge of God's revealed will is within our reach, and will do us good. Let man look upon this as his wisdom, To fear the Lord, and to depart from evil. Let him learn that, and he is learned enough. Where is this wisdom to be found? The treasures of it are hid in Christ, revealed by the word, received by faith, through the Holy Ghost. It will not feed pride or vanity, or amuse our vain curiosity. It teaches and encourages sinners to fear the Lord, and to depart from evil, in the exercise of repentance and faith, without desiring to solve all difficulties about the events of this life.
